projects.title: Label-free rice mapping under monsoon cloud
projects.summary: A rice map for 132 areas with no training labels: the optical crop calendar finds rice, the radar flooding signal confirms it.
projects.problem: Rice is grown in the cloudiest months of the year and no labelled fields existed, so a normal supervised model could not even start. A first radar-only draft looked convincing, but a pixel-by-pixel check against Sentinel-2 showed its key radar feature peaked after the crop had already been cut: it was measuring harvested fields, not the growing canopy.
data: Sentinel-2: 93 to 172 dates per AOI, composited into 5-day windows
Sentinel-1: 266 tracks, 12 to 18 passes each, ascending and descending
3,533 surveyed plots reported as standing rice
422,763 field polygons from a SAMGeo delineation pipeline
method: Composite cloud-masked Sentinel-2 into 5-day windows and report gaps instead of inventing them
Read each pixel's crop cycle: a long bare trough, a fast climb, a canopy still standing on the map date
Confirm the transplanting flood with a radar drop of at least 3 dB below the field's own dry level
Audit every radar pass: drop artefact passes where evergreen ground jumps 3 dB or more
Aggregate to field polygons with a second-opinion confidence flag, then review 430 fields by eye and fix 23 kinds of problems, each measured before adoption
results: Plot-interior recall of 99.3%, 99.4% and 98.4% in the main regions
Evergreen false positives cut from 7.1% to 0.0%
Rule on field-mean curves agrees with the pixel vote on 89.5% of field area
97% of rice field acres were seen clear within 30 days of the map date: standing rice is observed, not extrapolated
projects.lesson: Hard-coded thresholds do not survive real data. Shape, timing and rate of change of the crop curve matter more than any single value, and every number must say what it is compared against.

projects.title: Rice from radar alone
projects.summary: Where clouds block every optical image, a radar-only model reproduces the validated rice map on areas it never saw.
projects.problem: Some areas sit under cloud so heavy that no optical time series can be built at all. Could rice be mapped there from Sentinel-1 alone, and how well, measured honestly?
data: Both Sentinel-1 orbits merged into one series, a pass about every 6 days
Surveyed plots for recall, optical-defined negatives (evergreen, water, bare, cut fields)
The validated optical + radar map of all 132 AOIs as the teacher
method: 131 features per pixel: a fixed 6-day VH, VV and VH-VV series plus season summaries and a flood test
Train XGBoost on the teacher's confident classes only
Leave out whole AOIs and whole regions in cross-validation, because neighbouring pixels are near-copies and a random split flatters every number
results: Held-out plot recall of 97.6%, 97.1% and 95.6%
Scored on plots, on negatives and on acre agreement with the teacher for areas the model never saw
projects.lesson: How you split the data decides whether the score means anything.

projects.title: Province and national-scale sugarcane mapping
projects.summary: Standing sugarcane at 10 m for whole provinces from a season of radar and optical data, delivered as clean field polygons with acres.
projects.problem: Mills and agribusinesses need to know how much cane is still standing, across entire provinces, every season, with polygons they can use.
data: A season of Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical images
District and grid tiles across each province
method: LightGBM time-series model plus a colour model
A recall rule that adds young plant cane the model misses
Sieve and hole-fill, then polygons under 0.15 acres dropped
Province mosaic and province GeoPackage of cane polygons with acres
Resumable, Airflow-ready pipeline with state on S3: the province name is the only required input
results: Whole provinces mapped in one resumable run
National-scale sugarcane mapping of Thailand from Sentinel-1
October 2026: standing sugarcane mapped over 5 provinces in NE Thailand, about 776,000 acres at 10 m
Field-level output for one province: 124,000 delineated fields labelled and cleaned with size-aware rules
Blind test set (480 blocks, 3 reviewers): F1 0.91
projects.lesson: At province scale, resumability and clean state matter as much as the model.

projects.title: Field-level rice, sugarcane and cassava maps
projects.summary: One polygon per field with a crop class, built mainly from radar, checked and corrected with optical images and blind human review.
projects.problem: A client needed field-level crop maps for a district-sized area where monsoon cloud hides most optical images.
data: Every Sentinel-1 pass of two orbits, every Sentinel-2 date with all cloud masks
Ground points and field delineation polygons
DEM and rainfall
method: Monthly radar features plus crop-calendar features (flooded dates, lowest VH, canopy growth, regrowth)
XGBoost: rice vs not rice, then cane-cassava vs the rest
Blind reviews: analysts label pixels on evidence sheets without seeing the model, and every round becomes new training data and an honest test
Field polygons by majority rule, mixed fields cut with straight lines, no overlaps or touching geometry
Final Sentinel-2 QC and cane/cassava split
results: Delivered shapefile and GeoParquet, one feature per field with class and acres
Every geometry passed automated QC before delivery
projects.lesson: If reviewers can see the model's answer, the review is not a test.

projects.title: Twelve years of crop maps, 2014 to 2025
projects.summary: District-level maps of sugarcane, wheat, maize and rice for every year since 2014, for an international development agency.
projects.problem: Long-term crop statistics need consistent maps across years and sensors, including years before Sentinel-2 existed.
data: Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 time series
Training data built for each crop
method: NDVI every 8 days, Whittaker-smoothed per pixel, classified with Random Forest
A cloud-free static image classified with XGBoost only where the time-series model found the crop
Sieve and vectorise to polygons
Earth Engine or an open STAC catalogue, switchable in config, after the client could no longer use Earth Engine
results: Maps for every year from 2014 to 2025, accepted by the client
One pipeline instead of three diverging notebooks
projects.lesson: Make data sources swappable from day one: they change.

projects.title: Catching hidden model failures
projects.summary: Two production bugs that looked like good results: a validation split that hid a model's failure, and a date shift that inflated area by 63%.
metrics: true recall on a new date
projects.problem: A sugarcane model reported excellent scores, and a cotton pipeline produced plausible maps. Both were wrong in ways no metric showed.
data: Sentinel-2 acquisitions across the season
Training tables and inference configs
method: Sugarcane: the static model was trained on seven dates inside one three-week window, with a random per-pixel split. I tested it on other dates: recall fell from 85.0% (10 Aug) to 35.9% (4 Sep)
Rebuilt it with grouped validation, multi-date training and a domain-shift guard
Cotton: the inference window started one step late, so every feature was read 8 days off. Area jumped from 4.63% to 7.57% of the test area
Fixed the dates, added a guard that stops the run if dates do not match training, and wrote tests
results: A date-robust sugarcane classifier with honest validation
A cotton pipeline that refuses to run on mismatched dates
projects.lesson: A high score from a random pixel split is a question, not an answer.

projects.title: SAR maize mapping in the cloudy tropics
projects.summary: Leading radar research on maize detection in a persistently cloudy climate.
projects.problem: In persistently cloudy regions optical satellites miss the whole maize season.
data: Sentinel-1 GRD scenes
Ground-truth polygons
method: Master grid and chunking, track and gap audit including rain
Radiometric terrain flattening and preprocessing in Earth Engine per chunk and track
Download with integrity checks, per-date stacks and QA
Pixel explorer to compare any pixel's time series with ground truth
results: Analysis-ready multi-date VV + VH stacks and a pixel index for model development
projects.lesson: Audit tracks, dates and rain before modelling: radar has its own clouds.

projects.title: Field boundaries at scale
projects.summary: End-to-end field delineation built around Segment Anything (SAMGeo), plus tools for open boundaries and survey reconciliation.
projects.problem: Crop maps are only useful to farms and mills when they follow real field boundaries.
data: High-resolution and Sentinel imagery
Open Fields of The World boundaries
Surveyed field boundaries
method: Imagery preparation, SAMGeo segmentation, polygon cleaning and simplification
Fields of The World boundaries clipped, cleaned and measured for any area
Rules that reconcile model polygons with surveyed boundaries
Memory-bounded, resumable dissolve for 1.5M+ features
results: Pipeline used for sugarcane mapping in Thailand and South Africa
422,763 fields delineated for the Myanmar rice project
IoU of 0.995 against reference boundaries
Survey reconciliation: 566,090 acres and 123,357 polygons delivered for two sugarcane areas; 105k model polygons in ~15 min on 8 cores, resumable on spot machines
projects.lesson: Geometry quality is a deliverable, not an afterthought.

projects.title: Snowmelt prediction with machine and deep learning
projects.summary: 67 years of snowmelt (1948-2014) modelled from 38 variables; an LSTM reached R² 0.97. First-author paper in Water Resources Management.
projects.problem: Northern Pakistan depends on snowmelt for irrigation and drinking water, yet melt is driven by many interacting factors and is hard to predict.
data: GLDAS land data assimilation records, 1948 to 2014
38 independent variables including albedo, surface skin temperature, radiation fluxes, soil moisture and runoff
method: Data transformation and Recursive Feature Elimination to find key predictors
Linear Regression and Random Forest models
LSTM deep learning model for temporal dependencies
Feature importance analysis of the drivers of melt
results: LSTM: R² 0.9697, MAE 0.0035 kg m⁻²
Random Forest: R² 0.9263, RMSE 0.0094 kg m⁻², far ahead of Linear Regression
Key drivers: storm surface runoff, soil moisture content and ground heat flux
projects.lesson: This B.S. project grew into my first first-author journal paper.

projects.title: Glacial lake segmentation with deep learning
projects.summary: Multi-sensor fusion and deep segmentation models for mapping glacial lakes, a key input for outburst-flood risk.
projects.problem: Glacial lakes grow as glaciers retreat, and their outburst floods threaten downstream communities. Mapping them reliably across large mountain areas needs automation.
data: Sentinel-2 and other sensors fused for lake detection
method: U-Net, a simple CNN and ASPP-SegNet compared for semantic segmentation
Multi-sensor fusion of inputs
results: Published in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing (2025)

projects.title: Optical vs radar crop mapping (M.Phil. research)
projects.summary: A district-wide comparison of Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 for crop classification, including accuracy and computational cost.
projects.problem: Optical data is accurate but fails in the monsoon; radar works through cloud but is harder to read. Which should a mapping programme use, and at what cost?
data: Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 time series over a full district
Reference data at validation sites
method: Cloud and shadow masking, gap-filled NDVI with Whittaker smoothing
Classification with both sensors
Accuracy, Kappa and F1 per class, and field-level checks at four sites
Comparison of computational trade-offs
results: Optical 94.5% vs radar 86.8% overall accuracy
Radar kept working through the monsoon cloud gap

experience.role: Machine Learning Engineer and Team Lead
points: Lead a team of machine-learning and remote-sensing engineers delivering satellite crop-monitoring products to agribusinesses and development agencies in Asia, Africa and South America.

Myanmar rice: designed a label-free method (optical crop calendar + radar flood confirmation) across 132 AOIs, validated on 3,533 surveyed plots with plot-interior recall up to 99.4%; built a radar-only XGBoost model with 97.6% held-out recall for cloud-blocked areas.
Thailand: national-scale sugarcane mapping from Sentinel-1 radar; field delineation for sugar mills.
Pakistan: training data, models and pipeline for district-level crop maps of Punjab and Sindh for every year 2014 to 2025 (sugarcane, wheat, maize, rice, cotton).

FireBird: designed an automated deep-learning workflow that segments and vectorises field boundaries from open basemap imagery. CaneIntel and CaneCast: multi-year NDVI models that reconstruct sugarcane sowing history and forecast crop presence and type.
Built the end-to-end SAMGeo field-boundary pipeline used in Thailand, South Africa and Myanmar (422,763 fields in one project).
Phenology intelligence: an NDVI-trough method that finds sowing and harvest windows for rice, maize and sugarcane, feeding acreage and yield estimates.
Philippines: lead Sentinel-1 research on maize detection in a persistently cloudy climate. Brazil and Pakistan: NDVI time-series models for sugarcane sowing and harvest windows.
Found and fixed hidden failures: a random pixel split that hid a 35.9% recall on new dates, and a date-window bug that inflated cotton area by 63%.
Built a real-time GIS progress-monitoring dashboard for the WASA Lahore Development Project.
Built reusable spatial-analysis components for the project team.
Set up field-survey data collection and live ingestion through ODK Central.
Built high-resolution image classifiers and a deep-learning model for satellite image super-resolution.
Managed imagery quality assessment and ground-control planning.
Wrote Sentinel-2 and Google Earth Engine crop-classification scripts and an initial maize-detection model, which led to a full-time role.
